item.title: Generative AI: Chunking Strategies, Prompt Engineering & AWS Bedrock
item.author: ThanhLD
item.description: Core concepts in Generative AI architectures, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) chunking strategies, Prompt Engineering techniques, and AWS Bedrock services. RAG Chunking Strategies Chunking divides long documents into smaller segments for embedding and vector similarity search. 1. Fixed-Size Chunking (Standard) Concept: Chunks document into fixed token lengths (e.g. 300 - 512 tokens) with an overlap percentage (e.g. 10 - 20%). Pros: Fast, simple, predictable computation. Cons: Can cut sentences or paragraphs mid-thought, causing loss of semantic context.

item.title: JavaScript, TypeScript & React Core Concepts
item.author: ThanhLD
item.description: JavaScript Fundamentals Closures A closure in JavaScript allows the function to remember the variables from the enclosing function where it was created, enabling encapsulation and state retention. Hoisting Hoisting in JavaScript is a behavior where variable and function declarations are moved to the top of their containing scope during the compile phase, before the code is executed. This means that you can use variables and functions before they are declared in the code.

item.title: Golang Deep Dive: Concurrency, Runtime & Architecture
item.author: ThanhLD
item.description: In-depth technical notes on Go concurrency, memory management, garbage collection internals, performance profiling, hexagonal architecture, and design patterns. Concurrency & Channels Channel Types 1. Unbuffered Channel Behavior: An unbuffered channel has zero capacity (make(chan int)). Synchronization: Requires both sender and receiver to be ready at the exact same moment. Send blocks until a receiver is ready, and receive blocks until a sender is ready. Use Case: Strict point-to-point synchronization between goroutines.

item.title: Database & Message Brokers: SQL, NoSQL & Queues
item.author: ThanhLD
item.description: Comprehensive notes on Relational Databases (SQL), In-Memory Caching (Redis), and Distributed Message Brokers (Kafka & RabbitMQ) for technical interviews and system architecture design. Relational Databases (SQL) SQL vs NoSQL ACID Properties in Relational Databases Atomicity: All operations in a transaction succeed or fail together. If any operation fails, the entire transaction is rolled back. (e.g. transfer money from Account A to Account B). Consistency: Any transaction brings the database from one valid state to another, strictly obeying all schema rules, constraints, triggers, and cascades.
